finding: The spec-feedback report of ST-0431 misses one contract text that the re-dispatch fix changes. The first bullet of validation-rules.md § Dispatch ledger (line 169) says that re-dispatch is an idempotent no-op when the entry is already in the target state. Before ST-0431, re-dispatch of a prepared entry exited 0 and wrote nothing, because Ledger.transition returns early for the same state. Now cmd_re_dispatch refuses a prepared entry with exit 1, as the Contract table of the story asks. Row 2 of the report names only the re-dispatch bullet of interface-contracts.md § dispatch, so the domain-modeling agent can fix that bullet and leave the idempotency line as it is. Fix: add a row for docs/spec/validation-rules.md, Owner domain-modeling-agent, which says that re-dispatch is no longer a no-op on prepared and refuses it like pending, dispatching, dispatched and done, and that re-dispatch leaves the list of idempotent subcommands. Owner: developer-agent.
why_this_severity: The report already records that re-dispatch refuses prepared, so the owner who reads it learns the new behavior and no story builds from the stale line (no to fails_purpose); the idempotency line of validation-rules.md then contradicts the code until reconciliation finds it, and a reader must compare both to see which one holds (raises_cost). The report and the code exist only on story/ST-0431.
